scope: Bounded primary-paper and author-report inspection of definitions/comparison settings, not an exhaustive review

papers.paper: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
papers.authors: Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger
papers.original_task: Multiclass confidence calibration, image and document classifiers
papers.inputs: Predicted-class probability and correctness labels on evaluation items
papers.original_cost: One predictive distribution per item; binning aggregation, no additional model call to calculate ECE
papers.adaptation: Same fixed-bin functional on ARC chosen-option probabilities; ten bins frozen here. Used as one model-level source predictor, not target risk correction. Guo attributes ECE to earlier work, so not a novelty priority claim.
papers.why: Available from the same source responses and labels as other groups.

papers.paper: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability
papers.locator: Printed p.1, Verification Formula, Eq.(2); p.2 range discussion; first-page scan visually checked
papers.original_task: Probabilistic forecasts over mutually exclusive exhaustive categories
papers.inputs: Full class probability vector and realized class label
papers.original_cost: O(number of items times number of options) arithmetic after probabilities exist
papers.adaptation: Apply original summed multicategory form to all real ARC options; no division by class count; not (chosen_confidence-correctness)^2.
papers.why: Uses source option distribution already cached. Publisher403, original paper scan retrieved from university course mirror and verified.

papers.paper: A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks
papers.locator: Section 3, first two paragraphs, PDF p.3
papers.original_formula: MSP(x)=max_k softmax(z(x))_k; use -MSP for error-positive detection
papers.original_task: Per-example misclassification and OOD detection, AUROC/AUPR
papers.inputs: Single-example class logits/probabilities; evaluation labels needed to assess detection
papers.original_cost: One forward prediction, inexpensive probability reduction
papers.adaptation: Mean MSP is already C in source B. We do not claim our model-level MSE is directly comparable to the paper's per-example AUROC.
papers.why: No duplicate feature or redundant competitor is introduced.

papers.locator: Computer Sciences Technical Report1648, updated Jan26 2010; Section3.1 Uncertainty Sampling, printed pp.12–13
papers.original_task: Selecting informative examples for annotation, not confidence calibration
papers.inputs: Single class posterior vector; raw uncertainty score does not need its example label
papers.original_cost: Posterior reductions; labels needed later for active-learning updates, not for raw uncertainty score
papers.adaptation: Average over ARC items; entropy divided by log(number of real options), a declared normalization in our protocol. No acquisition or active-learning claim. Author-hosted technical report describes these standard definitions; we do not attribute their invention to Settles.
papers.why: Representative distribution summaries computable under identical cached input budget.

papers.paper: LM-Polygraph: Uncertainty Estimation for Language Models
papers.original_formula: P(sequence|x)=product_l P(y_l|y_<l,x); token/sequence entropy have different event spaces
papers.original_task: Uncertainty estimation for generated text, common software and benchmark
papers.inputs: Method-specific token probabilities, hidden states, generated texts or multiple model samples
papers.adaptation: Method taxonomy and resource accounting only. Our normalized option entropy is not a replication of mean token entropy, sequence entropy or semantic entropy.
papers.why: No additional method added solely because it appears in the toolkit.

papers.paper: Benchmarking Uncertainty Quantification Methods for Large Language Models with LM-Polygraph
papers.locator: TACL13:220–248; arXiv2406.15627v4; Table1, Section5.1 Selective QA/Generation and Section5.3 calibration
papers.original_formula: PRR=area(rejection_curve - random_curve)/area(oracle_curve - random_curve), subject to the paper's quality orientation
papers.original_task: Selective QA/generation, fact-checking and confidence calibration evaluated separately
papers.inputs: Predictions/uncertainty estimates plus task-specific correctness or quality labels
papers.original_cost: Method-dependent; common comparison environment reports resource categories
papers.adaptation: Supports distinguishing task and evaluation layers. PRR is not computed here: our frozen outcome is model-level R50 prediction, with one coverage.
papers.why: Context for fair comparisons; no borrowed SOTA claim or direct numerical benchmark comparison.

papers.paper: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
papers.locator: Section2, Eq.(1) and empirical definitions, PDF pp.3–4
papers.original_task: Selective classification, trading coverage and risk with target risk control
papers.inputs: Prediction, selection score/function and validation labels
papers.original_cost: Selection/calibration on model predictions; their statistical guarantee depends on their design
papers.adaptation: Our R50 is empirical 0–1 selective risk at exactly ceil(N/2) selected by existing confidence. Parameters predict this scalar; no new per-item rejector or transferred risk guarantee.
papers.why: Defines the intended risk, not an additional predictor family.

papers.paper: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
papers.original_formula: P(True)=probability assigned to truth of a supplied proposed answer under an explicit self-evaluation prompt
papers.original_task: Self-evaluation of generated answers and calibration of that evaluation
papers.inputs: Answer generation plus explicit True/False/self-evaluation continuation; variants use additional samples
papers.original_cost: Additional model processing beyond the original option-response cache
papers.adaptation: None; no corresponding self-evaluation logits exist in the authorized inputs.
papers.why: Cannot substitute chosen-option probability for P(True); not tested and no claim of superiority or measured cost speedup against it.

papers.paper: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
papers.authors: Lorenz Kuhn, Yarin Gal, Sebastian Farquhar
papers.locator: Sections3–4; generation/clustering/entropy steps, PDF pp.4–5; AppendixD margin comparison
papers.original_formula: H_sem=-sum_c P(c|x)log P(c|x), P(c|x)=sum_{s in semantic class c}P(s|x), estimated using generated samples
papers.original_task: Uncertainty of meanings in free-form QA
papers.inputs: Multiple generated answers, sequence probabilities, bidirectional entailment grouping
papers.original_cost: Repeated generation and entailment inference, beyond fixed-option caches
papers.adaptation: Not implemented. AppendixD also gives a top-two sequence likelihood margin; our margin is over fixed option probabilities, not beam outputs.
papers.why: Missing authorized generation/semantic inputs; no empirical comparison or cost superiority claim.
